title: NVML symbol shadowing & libcuda mixing — bisect log
content:
Summary:
This is a scratch log for a recurring class of failures where user processes hit GPU OOMs or NVML errors that look like driver/library symbol mismatches. Symptoms are intermittent across containers and nodes. Suspect: multiple copies of driver/NVML/libcuda on host vs container (symbol versioning / shadowing), plus an edge case of ldconfig/ld.so.cache returning unexpected lib paths after package changes or image layer changes.

Environment notes (repro targets):
- Nodes: ubuntu-22.04, kernel 6.1.63-rt (custom infra), driver: 535.86.10 (rpm installed on host)
- nvidia-container-toolkit: v1.12.0; nvidia-docker/nvidia-container-runtime in use
- Containers: various base images (debian:12, ubuntu:22.04); some images built with CUDA toolkit tarballs (11.8, 12.1) in /usr/local/cuda-*/lib64 included in image layers
- Workload: PyTorch 2.1 / transformers script; common entrypoint: python -u serve.py --model XX

Minimal repro (quick check):
1) docker run --rm --gpus all -it --entrypoint bash my-image:latest
2) python - <<'PY'
import torch
print('torch', torch.__version__)
print('cuda available', torch.cuda.is_available())
import pynvml
pynvml.nvmlInit()
print('nvml ok')
PY
Expected: nvmlInit succeeds. Observed: stack trace like below.

Observed errors (collected snippets):
- Python stack:
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/pynvml.py", line 240, in nvmlInit
    _nvmlInit()
  OSError: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1: undefined symbol: nvmlEventSetAllocNotifyCallback

- dmesg/syslog: kernel: NVRM: GPU at 00000000:01:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
- nvidia-smi reports driver mismatch sometimes: "Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch"

Quick ldd / readelf checks (commands I ran):
- ldd $(python -c 'import pynvml,sys;print(pynvml.__file__)')
  -> shows libnvidia-ml.so.1 -> /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libnvidia-ml.so (stubs) or /opt/vendor/lib/libnvidia-ml.so.1 depending on image
- readelf -s libnvidia-ml.so.1 | grep nvmlEventSetAllocNotifyCallback
  -> symbol present in host /usr/lib but missing in container-stubbed copy
- find / -name libnvidia-ml.so* -print shows multiple copies: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/, /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/stubs/, /opt/conda/pkgs/cuda-toolkit-*/lib/

Commands tried (sequence and rationale):
1) Confirm driver loaded on host: sudo nvidia-smi -> OK (driver 535)
2) docker run --gpus all --rm --privileged busybox sh -c 'ls -l /proc/driver/nvidia/ctk' -> confirms driver files present in proc
3) inside container: ldconfig -p | grep nvidia -> shows stubs first (broken order)
4) ldd of python extension modules (torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so) -> shows they pick up /usr/local/cuda-*/lib64/libcuda.so -> sometimes the stub, sometimes the real symlink depending on image layering
5) strace on python import pynvml to see which lib is opened: strace -f -e openat python -c 'import pynvml' -> openat shows container layer file paths
6) nm -D /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 | grep nvmlEventSetAllocNotifyCallback -> present on host but not in stubbed files

Hypotheses: 
- Some images include CUDA toolkit libs (libcuda/libnvidia-ml) from the toolkit tarball (stubs or partial impl). When the container runtime mounts /usr/lib or otherwise allows host driver libs, ld.so resolution picks the wrong copy (stub vs. real) leading to missing symbol at runtime.
- An older container image built with mismatched toolkit (11.8) plus newer host driver (535) can still succeed normally, but in specific code paths (alloc notify event APIs) the symbol is required and missing -> OSError "undefined symbol".
- LD_LIBRARY_PATH or LD_PRELOAD tricks used in quick fixes introduced additional copies earlier in search path and made behaviour inconsistent across restarts.
- nvidia-container-toolkit version differences change mount order of driver libs into container; upgrades/downgrades have caused breakage in the past.

Temporary mitigations tested (results):
- set LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu (host path) inside container -> sometimes fixes NVML init, but breaks other things that expect toolkit libs (cuBLAS from /usr/local/cuda)
- remove /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libnvidia-ml.so from image and rebuild -> reliably fixes on that image (good sign)
- docker run --volume /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/host-nvidia-lib:ro ... and LD_PRELOAD=/host-nvidia-lib/libnvidia-ml.so.1 -> works for nvmlInit, but is a hack and fails under some orchestrators
- upgrading nvidia-container-toolkit to latest (1.12.0) on node -> mixed results; I think mount ordering changed between 1.11.x and 1.12.x depending on distro packaging

Recommended long-term fixes to try in next iterations: 
- Make a small Dockerfile base image that intentionally contains NO driver/toolkit libs (only CUDA headers or nothing). Validate that running it always picks host libs. Publish as our base runtime.
- Add a runtime-time assertion in startup that verifies nvml event symbols exist: readelf -s $(ldconfig -p | grep libnvidia-ml.so.1 | head -1 | awk '{print $4}') | grep nvmlEventSetAllocNotifyCallback and fail early with clear error message listing all discovered copies and their symbol table status.
- Update CI image build step to fail if /usr/local/cuda/lib64 contains libnvidia-ml.so* (toolkit stubs) accidentally baked in.
- Work with infra to standardize nvidia-container-toolkit version across fleet and coordinate driver upgrades so host+toolkit semantics are consistent.

Debug checklist (copy / paste):
- On host: sudo nvidia-smi && modinfo nvidia | grep version && ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1
- Inside container: python -c 'import ctypes,ctypes.util;print(ctypes.util.find_library("nvidia-ml"))'
- strace -f -e openat python -c 'import pynvml' 2>&1 | grep libnvidia-ml
- readelf -s $(python -c 'import ctypes.util,sys;print(ctypes.util.find_library("nvidia-ml"))') | grep nvmlEventSetAllocNotifyCallback || echo MISSING
- find / -name 'libnvidia-ml.so*' -exec readlink -f {} \; -print

Unresolved / next experiments:
- Reproduce on fresh node from image: still intermittent. Need to capture exact mount table at container start (use nsenter to check mounts)
- Confirm whether driver upgrade on host (535->540) changes whether symbol present in libnvidia-ml.so.1 when mounted into container from host vs image
- Try building a tiny static test binary that calls nvmlEventSetAllocNotifyCallback to force link-time check and run it in different images to see deterministic fail mode

Notes to self:
- Avoid LD_PRELOAD as a long-term fix; tends to mask and move the problem.
- If you see "Driver/library version mismatch" from NVML, check for multiple libnvidia-ml copies first (stubs vs real).
- When in doubt, capture: strace open paths, readelf symbol tables, and the container mount list (cat /proc/self/mountinfo) at failure time.

Raw command snippets I've saved (for quick run):
- strace -f -e openat python -c 'import pynvml' 2>&1 | grep nvidia || true
- for p in $(find / -name 'libnvidia-ml.so*' 2>/dev/null); do echo "==== $p ==="; readelf -s $p | grep nvmlEventSetAllocNotifyCallback || echo MISSING; done
- python - <<'PY'
import ctypes.util,sys
print('ctypes find', ctypes.util.find_library('nvidia-ml'))
PY

Quick timeline (notes):
- 2026-02-28: First customer hit on k8s cluster A; initial mitigation was container rebuild without CUDA toolkit files baked in (worked)
- 2026-03-01: Reappeared on cluster B where old base image was cached on nodes; suspect image layered in via CRI caching
- 2026-03-05: Began bisecting images, confirmed removing stubs fixes consistently
- 2026-03-10: Found one customer image with libnvidia-ml.so.1 symlinked to a stale conda pkg file -> cleaned and resolved

Open questions to triage with infra / images team: 
- Which build pipelines still include CUDA toolkit tarballs by default? Can we opt-out?
- Can the container runtime be made to always bind-mount host driver libs at a PATH-preferred location so stubs inside images are never picked?
- Are there older driver packages lingering on nodes that could clash with newer drivers during hot upgrades?

TL;DR: Most of these failures trace back to multiple copies of libnvidia-ml/libcuda in the combined host+container filesystem, leading ld.so to pick a copy missing newer NVML symbols. Best short-term action: prevent toolkit stubs from being baked into runtime images and add a startup check that fails fast with a clear diagnostic listing all libnvidia-ml copies and whether required symbols are present.
